title: Mastering Pagination UX
summary: This lesson explores essential pagination strategies for data tables, including choosing the right pattern for user needs and solving technical issues like data drift. It covers cursor-based pagination, UI truncation, scroll restoration, and URL state management.

transcript.text: Offset pagination hides a bug. Add one row at the top and every page shifts down.
People see the same item twice.
Cursors fix the drift. Paginate by after this ID, not skip 500.
The list stays stable as data changes.
Three patterns. Each one fits a different job.
Numbered for jumping, load more for control, infinite for feeds.
Each one fits a different job.
Do not render 500 page links. Truncate.
First, a gap, the current pages, a gap, the last. Always keep first and last reachable.
Get back from a detail page. Land on the row you left, not at the top.
Restore scroll, or you lose your place.
Put the page number in the URL. Page 500 becomes a link you can share or refresh.
State lives in the address bar.
Follow for more UI systems. Save this for your next data table.

design_principles: Use cursor-based pagination to prevent item duplication and drift in dynamic lists.
Select pagination patterns based on user goals: Numbered for specific access, Load More for manual control, and Infinite Scroll for discovery.
Truncate long pagination ranges to avoid UI overflow while keeping the first and last pages accessible.
Implement scroll restoration to maintain user context when navigating back from detail views.
Sync UI state with the URL to enable deep linking and persistent views across refreshes.
before_after: Demonstrates the transition from buggy offset pagination to stable cursor pagination, and from cluttered link lists to clean, truncated navigation with URL state persistence.
